invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the validated PreparedLaunch stage's required capability set against the driver's declared conformed capabilities; both are complete at the driver-entry boundary and need no external probe. Q2: declared driver capabilities live at the driver/provider boundary, so runtime owns them. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because the next act is a native effect. Q4: the caller-facing synchronous rejection of a capability-gated live request is a different owner on the live traversal and is already carried by the existing live-capability entry. Reject-at-boundary: the capability declaration is static driver metadata.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the typed capability-unsupported result before effect-producing work instead of substituting an approximate native mechanism.

invariants.title: Driver widens, narrows, or downgrades the requested postcondition
invariants.statement: A driver's native lowering of a Core method establishes exactly the requested postcondition and never a colder, wider, or more destructive fallback.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the requested postcondition carried by the validated PreparedLaunch stage together with the declared postcondition and effect class of each native step; both are complete at the driver-entry boundary. Q2: native step selection at the driver/provider boundary is the runtime owner. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because the native effect follows immediately. Q4: the public-surface rule that a method must have one exact postcondition is a Core fact set filed separately; this entry constrains the lowering, not the naming. Reject-at-boundary: the declared postcondition of each native step is static driver metadata.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the operation as unsupported rather than lowering it to a native step whose postcondition differs from the requested one.

invariants.title: Driver advertises Core Exec without full execution conformance
invariants.statement: A driver advertises Core Exec only when it proves a targetable execution containment unit covering the Process and its owned descendants, durable output spooling with stable byte cursors and explicit truncation, exact terminal evidence, stdin ownership and close semantics, provable Process termination, and adoption of the same attempted execution after control-plane failure.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the driver's declared conformance evidence for those six requirements; that evidence is static driver metadata complete at the driver-entry boundary and needs no runtime observation. Q2: driver conformance declarations live at the driver/provider boundary. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because advertising Exec makes the Core admit Exec requests against this target. Q4: the individual Process I/O and termination rules are separate entries on the exec traversal; this entry governs admission of the driver to the Exec surface. Reject-at-boundary: the conformance declaration is available before any effect.

diagnostic.remediation: Supply a Core-managed in-guest supervisor and durable spool, or do not advertise full Core Exec for this target.

invariants.title: Artifact asserts a dynamic Core or runtime fact
invariants.statement: An Artifact Definition declares only frontend-independent static facts and cannot express current Sandbox or Process state, current runtime epoch or etag, resource capacity, provider admission, concurrent Operations, Snapshot retention or reference state, expiration races, provider availability, or evidence freshness.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the resolved Artifact Definition's field set against the closed set of declarative facts; that is complete once the Artifact is semantically resolved, and no runtime observation refines it. Q2: Artifact Definition content is owned by artifact. Q3: the build station is the last correct refusal point, because a built manifest that asserts a dynamic fact is thereafter treated as authoritative. Q4: the conformance-evidence instance and the host-path instance extend existing target and Artifact entries and are not refiled here. Unrepresentable because no Artifact schema field can name a current Core or runtime fact.

diagnostic.remediation: Express the dynamic condition as a runtime precondition on the Core operation and keep the Artifact limited to declarative facts.

invariants.title: Start accepted against a Sandbox without a durable stopped proof
invariants.statement: `StartSandbox` is admitted only against a Sandbox holding a current durable stopped proof, and never restarts a runtime that is still present under an unretired epoch.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Start request and the Sandbox's current durable stopped proof, both complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Sandbox, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a second runtime from being launched over an unretired epoch. Q4: the offending act is the StartSandbox request, so it stays on the live traversal. Filed under L0.D0: the packet avoided the forbidden C0→R1 shape by dropping StartSandbox coverage rather than filing it correctly.

diagnostic.remediation: Observe a current durable stopped proof before issuing StartSandbox; stop the present runtime and let its epoch retire first.

invariants.title: Launch dispatched without operator re-admission of its resolved placement
invariants.statement: A launch is dispatched only after the operator admission plane re-admits its resolved placement, capacity, and tier for the current epoch; a placement admitted for a prior launch never carries forward.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved placement, capacity, and tier for the current epoch and the operator admission plane's current admission record, complete from operator re-admission. Q2: operator capability and placement admission are the operator boundary. Q3: D0 is the dispatch station and the last point at which an unadmitted placement can be refused. Q4: the offending act is this launch's own dispatch. Filed under L0.D0; `O0` was used as a firstSoundPhase by zero of the 204 draft entries.

diagnostic.remediation: Re-admit the resolved placement, capacity, and tier at the operator admission plane for the current epoch before dispatching the launch.

invariants.title: Statically absent cross-target capability deferred to launch without an explicit target branch
invariants.statement: A cross-target capability, semantic, or ceiling that is statically absent from an enabled target is rejected during Artifact validation unless the Artifact declares an explicit named target branch for it, and is never deferred to workload launch or runtime discovery.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Artifact's enabled target set and the statically declared capability, semantic, and ceiling surfaces of each target, all complete at Artifact authoring and validation. Q2: declarative static facts are the Artifact boundary. Q3: A1 is the validation station and the last point at which a statically absent capability can be refused before launch. Q4: the offending act is the Artifact authoring itself. Added under L2.D15: TAXONOMY-46 is struck from `144`, which does not state it, and is filed here with RESULT-44.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare an explicit named target branch in the Artifact for every statically absent cross-target capability, semantic, or ceiling instead of deferring it to launch or runtime discovery.

invariants.title: Stale provider event treated as serialization authority
invariants.statement: A decoded provider, host, or VMM event is retained as non-authoritative evidence and is refused as a state transition whenever the authority epoch it belongs to is no longer current.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the event, the authority epoch it was produced under, and the current authority epoch, all present at the decoding boundary. Q2: decoding provider events is the driver/provider boundary, which is runtime; the Core commit rule is a separate two-owner seam. Q3: D0 is the decoding boundary and the last station where the event can still be downgraded to evidence. Q4: the offending act is the driver's decode, not the caller's request.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject the transition by authority epoch and retain the event only as protected non-authoritative evidence.

invariants.title: Incompatible concurrent lifecycle mutations both receive authority
invariants.statement: At most one nonterminal Operation holds the fenced Sandbox lifecycle-mutation lane, and a request whose ordered operation pair with the lane holder is not an explicitly permitted row of the compatibility ledger is refused with the typed conflict naming that active Operation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable lane record, the incoming request's kind and target, and the reviewed compatibility row for that ordered pair, all complete at the live admission station L0 with no external probe. Q2: the lane record and Operation acceptance are Core durable facts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusal is correct, because acceptance durably grants the lane and both mutations then hold authority; the loser of the Resume-versus-Stop race is decided by which request durably acquires the lane here. Q4: the offending operation is the second request itself, whose own admission this entry describes. `reject-at-boundary` under Ruling R2 because lane occupancy is a Core durable record. Ledger totality — that no pair row may be absent and none may inherit from a provider verb — has no traversal answer to the first two questions and is carried as a ledger validator rule, not duplicated here.

diagnostic.remediation: Wait for or cancel the active lifecycle Operation, or issue a pair the compatibility ledger explicitly permits.

invariants.title: Unsupported capability approximated at creation
invariants.statement: A creation requiring a capability-gated Core behavior resolves a target profile advertising that exact conformed capability, and an unadvertised capability is rejected rather than approximated by a different mechanism, a weaker guarantee, or a provider default.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the creation's required capability set and the effective capabilities of the resolved member and runtime profile, which first exist together where the verified manifest and the CreateSandbox input meet at C0; no host or provider state is consulted, since capability advertisement is an immutable resolved fact. Q2: the creation request surface owns the resolution, so the owner is `create`. Q3: C0, the last station at which refusal is correct, because the resolved creation passes to operator placement and driver preparation immediately afterwards and an approximation made there is invisible to the caller. Q4: the same creation commits the violation; the live-request half of this obligation is a different owner and station and is carried by the existing live capability entry.

diagnostic.remediation: Select a profile advertising the exact conformed capability, or drop the capability-gated requirement from the creation.

invariants.statement: A creation whose resolved `initialRuntime` is `stopped` commits a durable Sandbox whose runtime state is `stopped` and never enters `provisioning` or performs a launch effect.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved initial-runtime selection and the Sandbox record being committed, both complete at C0; the driver, host, and provider are never consulted for a creation that must not launch. Q2: the durable creation commit and the dispatch of a launch effect are the control plane's own artefacts. Q3: C0, because the resolved creation is handed to operator placement and host preflight immediately after, and a stopped creation that reaches those stations has already begun the launch it must not perform. Q4: this same creation commits the violation. `reject-at-boundary` because the creation boundary holds every fact needed to refuse.

invariants.title: Caller writes Sandbox runtime, desired state, or a presentation label
invariants.statement: Sandbox `status` -- its `runtime`, `execution`, `lifecycleOperation`, and `conditions` members -- is an output-only projection: no public request type carries a runtime state, a caller-writable desired runtime state, or a verb-derived presentation label as input, so every lifecycle change is an explicit named command and never a reconciled declaration.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared shape of the public live request types and the Sandbox `status` projection, both complete at semantic decoding. Q2: owner was contested between `live` and `core` and is resolved to `live` by Criterion O -- the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station. Q3: L0 is the decoding station and the only point at which the input can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's own request. Merged with index 127 (L0.D6, L1.D1, L2.D6, L3.D7 ref). This entry carries the request-input clause of LIFECYCLE-03; the storage/serialization-oracle clause is carried by the M11 survivor at L1, its own station -- the clause partition L0.D7 and L1.D19 asked for.

diagnostic.remediation: Issue the named lifecycle operation that produces the wanted state and read status as an observation, or declare desired state in a Managed-Sandbox Service that issues the same Core operations.

invariants.title: Verb-derived presentation label stored as Sandbox state
invariants.statement: Sandbox runtime state is exactly one of `provisioning`, `running`, `suspended`, `stopped`, or `unknown`; every derived presentation label -- creating, starting, suspending, resuming, stopping, restoring, deleting, snapshotting, migrating -- is recomputed at read time from the durable Operation and that authoritative status, and is never independently stored or used as the serialization oracle.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable Operation kind and the authoritative Core runtime status at the Operation and status commit station. Q2: the protected artefact is the Core durable status record and its serialization oracle, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1 is the commit station at which a stored presentation label would first become durable. Q4: the offending act is the lifecycle mutation's own commit. Merged from indices 101 and 128 (L0.D7, L1.D19, L2.D11). This entry carries only the storage/oracle clause of LIFECYCLE-03; the request-input clause is at the M2 survivor at L0, its own station. Reclassified 2026-08-03 from `unrepresentable`: the status type must carry a presentation label for the legitimate derivation, so forbidding the STORED case is a comparison against current state, not a variant that fails to exist. diagnostic.remediation: Derive presentation words at read time from the Operation kind and the authoritative status, and store neither.

invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the post-effect quiescence, continuity, and admission evidence for this Suspend, which exist only after the suspend effect has been applied, at the live-mutation resolution station L1. Q2: publishing the terminal outcome and the `suspended` status is a Core durable-record act, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1, the station at which the Operation terminalizes; refusing later is not a correct implementation because the caller has already been told the Sandbox is suspended. Q4: the same Suspend commits the violation. `observed-conformance` because the predicate is provable only from evidence returned after the effect.

diagnostic.remediation: Publish `suspended` only from returned quiescence and same-epoch continuity evidence; otherwise terminalize the Suspend as failed or unresolved.

invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's native continuity probes and their decoded results for this transition, which exist only after the driver has performed it, at L1. Q2: producing and decoding native evidence at the driver/provider boundary is owned by `runtime`, which is why this is a separate entry from the Core rule that consumes the evidence. Q3: L1, because the driver's report is what the Core terminalization consumes and there is no later driver station on this traversal. Q4: the driver acts within this same Suspend or Resume. `observed-conformance` because the evidence exists only post-effect.

diagnostic.remediation: Return the target's continuity probes with the report, and report failure when the target cannot prove same-epoch retention.

Q3: L1, because success published there is the false claim itself. Q4: the same Resume commits the violation. `observed-conformance` because continuity is provable only after the resume effect.

diagnostic.remediation: Terminalize a Resume that observed a cold fallback as failed or unresolved and leave any replacement to an explicitly authorized Start.

invariants.title: Stopped resize claims current provider capacity
invariants.statement: A `ResizeSandboxResources` Operation against a `stopped` Sandbox commits the validated concrete allocation for the next Start only, allocating no runtime epoch and claiming no current provider capacity.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the validated allocation and the Sandbox's stopped runtime record; the rule is decided from Core records alone with no external probe. Q2: the durable allocation record is owned by `core`. Q3: L1, the commit station for this live mutation, after which the allocation is published as if reserved. Q4: the same resize commits the violation. `reject-at-boundary` rather than `observed-conformance` because no post-effect evidence is required, and rather than `dynamic-preflight` under Ruling R2 because the allocation record is a Core durable fact.

diagnostic.remediation: Commit the next-Start allocation and report no epoch, reservation, or current capacity for a stopped Sandbox.

invariants.title: Stop lowered to a destructive provider delete
invariants.statement: A driver lowering `StopSandbox` uses only native steps that end the current runtime epoch and establish containment absence for it, leaving the logical Sandbox and its retained state intact, and never substitutes a provider delete, destroy, permanent kill, or other destructive removal.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the lowering the driver actually chose for one StopSandbox and the native steps the target exposes, both complete at driver lowering. Q2: the invalid state is an unproven driver claim about how a Core postcondition is realized, so the owner is `runtime` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a destructive removal from being dispatched under a Stop. Q4: the offending act is the lowering chosen on the live Stop traversal. Merged with index 139, a verbatim-title duplicate of one underlying problem (L0.D9, L1.D0, L2.D1, L3.D6); the merged content takes ADM's containment-absence framing onto the SBX index so neither statement is lost. Not folded into `142` (runtime, D0->D0, driver postcondition fidelity): under Criterion P the fact sets differ, since `142` reads the driver's declared postcondition contract at the launch-branch driver station while this entry reads the lowering actually chosen for one Stop on the live traversal, which never reaches D0.

diagnostic.remediation: Lower Stop to close-admission, revoke-launch, drain, terminate, and prove-absence steps against the current epoch, reject the target profile when only a destructive removal exists, and let the caller issue DeleteSandbox separately.

Q2: the published runtime state is a Core durable record, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1, because the approximation becomes authoritative the moment it is committed and would then admit Exec or successor authority. Q4: the same lifecycle mutation commits the approximation. `observed-conformance` because insufficiency of proof is established only from post-effect evidence.

invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the decoded provider vocabulary and the closed Core runtime-state vocabulary, both complete at the driver decoding boundary D0 with no further observation required. invariants.title: Launch succeeds before control, conformance, and admission are proven

invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the launch evidence set for the exact new epoch, including the control-attachment, conformance, and admission probe results, which exist only at the launch resolution station R1. Q2: publishing an Operation as `succeeded` is a terminal-outcome act, which resolves the recorded owner disagreement in favour of `core`. Q3: R1, the last station on the launch traversal at which withholding success is correct. Q4: the launch this entry describes commits the violation; the rule is filed as an R1 self-pair rather than the forbidden C0-to-R1 pair, because resolution-stage components do not revalidate a launch postcondition. `observed-conformance` because the postcondition is provable only after launch.

diagnostic.remediation: Publish launch success only after all declared control, conformance, and admission probes pass for the exact new epoch.

invariants.title: Provider-driven expiry relabeled a successful Core Stop or Delete
invariants.statement: An unpreventable provider expiry, idle stop, or reclamation is recorded as an uncontrolled provider-loss event requiring reconciliation, never retrospectively as a successful Core Stop or Delete.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the observed provider-initiated termination and the absence of a Core Operation whose postcondition it could discharge, available only once the loss is observed on the reconciliation traversal at R1. Q2: classifying the event and writing the durable outcome are Core acts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: R1, the station at which the reconciliation Operation terminalizes; relabelling committed there is the false claim. Q4: the reconciliation traversal that observes the loss is the one described, and under the system-origin ruling it is filed at its caller-originated twin's station. `observed-conformance` because the classification rests on post-launch observation.

diagnostic.remediation: Record the provider loss as its own event and reconcile the runtime state instead of crediting a Core Stop or Delete.

Q2: epoch sequencing and admission are Core durable records, so the owner is `core`. Q3: R1, the last station at which the Core can refuse to open admission; after admission opens, a Process is already bound to an unsequenced runtime. Q4: the reconciliation traversal that observes the wake is the one described, and a later Exec against the unsequenced epoch is filed on its own traversal. `observed-conformance` because the replacement is provable only from post-launch observation.

diagnostic.remediation: Sequence the observed runtime as a new epoch and open execution admission only after that record is durable.

invariants.statement: A durable stdout, stderr, or merged-terminal output cursor advances only after the bytes it covers are durably persisted.

Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because a published cursor is a promise of replayability that callers immediately rely on. diagnostic.remediation: Persist the byte range durably, then advance the cursor that covers it.

invariants.title: Cross-stream ordering promised without an explicitly merged terminal stream
invariants.statement: stdout and stderr have independent monotonic cursors that preserve ordering within each stream, and no cross-stream ordering is promised unless the accepted Exec selected a terminal that explicitly merges them.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted Exec's stream contract and the cursor structure being published; both are complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the stream contract and its cursors are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because publishing a single interleaved cursor is what creates the false promise. Q4: same traversal. Unrepresentable because the generated output type exposes per-stream cursors and offers a merged stream only for a Process whose accepted contract selected a merging terminal.

diagnostic.remediation: Read each stream from its own cursor, and request a terminal at Exec when merged ordering is required.

invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the composite's declared step sequence and the closed Core method union; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: explicit composites are named as adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core rule excluding compound public verbs from the method surface is a separate admission entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the composite's shape is fixed before the first Core call and each constituent call the Core sees is individually valid. Q4: the concealment is performed by the adapter on its own traversal.

diagnostic.remediation: Issue and surface each named Core operation and its Operation handle separately, and label the composite as an adapter helper.

invariants.title: Desired-state reconciler reaches the Core without etag and epoch preconditions or hides its system-originated Operations
invariants.statement: A managed desired-state reconciler reaches the Core only by issuing named Core operations under etag and runtime-epoch preconditions, and exposes its system-originated Operations for observation.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the reconciler's declared action set and record model together with the Core Operation and lifecycle contract; both are complete at the Managed-Sandbox Service Definition station, so firstSoundPhase is S0. Q2: the managed layer is the Managed-Sandbox Service Definition owner, so the owner is service. Q3: L0 is the last station on this same traversal at which refusing is still correct, because a reconciler action that reaches the Core as a live request must be refused there if it carries no etag or runtime-epoch precondition; S0 to L0 is a direct edge. Q4: the unguarded Core action and the concealment are performed by the managed controller, so they are filed on the managed traversal; the reconciler's rewriting of a predecessor Operation's terminal result is filed separately at `196`, and the core filing of system-originated Operations at their caller-originated twin's phase remains a separate core entry.

diagnostic.remediation: Issue named Core operations under etag and runtime-epoch preconditions, and expose the reconciler's system-originated Operations for observation.

invariants.title: Managed desired-state revision or restart policy carried in a Core request field
invariants.statement: A managed layer's desired-state revision and its restart/recreate policy live in the managed layer's own records; no Core request type carries either, so the Core never becomes a perpetual desired-state orchestrator.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared shape of the Core request types and the managed layer's own desired-state records, both complete at the service station. Q2: the Managed-Sandbox Service boundary owns its desired-state records, so the owner is `service`. Q3: S0 is the service station and the only point at which the unrepresentable input can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the managed layer's own request shape. Split out as clause (a) of `203` (L1.D17); `S0→S0` is introduced by this entry.

diagnostic.remediation: Keep the desired-state revision and the restart/recreate policy in the managed layer's own records and drive the Core only through named Core operations.

invariants.title: Reconciler rewrites a predecessor Operation's terminal result
invariants.statement: A reconciler that must correct a completed Core action appends a new linked successor Operation and never rewrites, reopens, or reinterprets a predecessor Operation's committed terminal result.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the predecessor Operation's committed terminal result and the correction the reconciler proposes, both complete from the service station through live admission. Q2: the reconciler's own conduct against the Core surface is the Managed-Sandbox Service boundary, so the owner is `service`. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a rewrite request can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the reconciler's request. Split out as clause (c) of `203` (L1.D17).

diagnostic.remediation: Append a new linked successor Operation instead of rewriting, reopening, or reinterpreting a predecessor's committed terminal result.

invariants.title: Creation rejection outside the sealed error registry
invariants.statement: Every synchronous rejection of a creation request is exactly one variant of the sealed public `RequestError` or `RecoveryError` registry admitted by that method's generated subset, with no catch-all variant, open string reason, arbitrary metadata reason, or provider-defined code.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the sealed registry, this method's exact generated subset, and the variant being emitted; all are known at the creation request surface. Q2: Core owns the closed error registry and the per-method admissibility sets, even though the station is the creation ingress. Q3: C0 is where the creation rejection is authored and returned. Q4: an adapter-added variant is committed by the adapter and is filed on the framework traversal. Filed per surface: one filing would claim that live and exec response encoders revalidate a pair they never traverse. `unrepresentable` because the generated per-method union admits no other value.

diagnostic.remediation: Add the condition to the sealed registry and regenerate the method subset, or map it onto an existing admitted variant.

Q2: Core owns the semantic result and the generated projection table. Q3: C0 is the emission station and the last point at which a projection inversion can be refused. Q4: an SDK that reinterprets its own local transport failure commits that outside Core and is filed on the framework traversal. `reject-at-boundary`: the projection is a table lookup over facts already held.

diagnostic.remediation: Derive the status from the product variant; return accepted work as its durable Operation with a successful transport status.

invariants.title: Restored or forked runtime admits execution without a successor Process contract
invariants.statement: A restored, restore-as-created, or forked runtime admits execution only through a newly allocated durable Core Process carrying its own identity, provenance, deadline, termination-request handling, containment, stdin ownership, durable output cursors, and terminal-evidence contract.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the launched runtime's observed execution units against the Core Process records allocated for the new epoch; those observations exist only after launch. Q2: durable Process identity and its control contract are Core durable records. Q3: the launch result station is the last correct point to refuse success, because publishing the new epoch as usable while an unowned execution acts would leave an uncontrollable workload. Q4: the v1 rejectNonterminal admission rule for capture is a different fact set on the capture request's own traversal. Disposition is observed-conformance because only post-launch observation can show an acting execution without a Core Process.

diagnostic.remediation: Reject capture while any Core Process is nonterminal, and reintroduce execution in the new epoch through a fresh Exec that allocates a durable Process.

invariants.statement: A launch against an existing Sandbox -- StartSandbox, same-Sandbox Restore, or restore-as-create -- acts only under the newly allocated runtime epoch and never grants, restores, or re-enables mutation authority to any epoch that preceded it.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durably allocated new epoch, the Sandbox's monotonic epoch high-water mark, and the authority grant the launch is about to make; all three are complete at the effect-authority station of the launch traversal, so firstSoundPhase is R0. invariants.title: Snapshot class identity disagrees with its resolved kind, components, or treatments
invariants.statement: A Snapshot's resolved class identity agrees with its declared kind, captured component set, external-storage state, secret treatment, compatibility envelope, quiescence state, device state, portability, and Process handling; any disagreement fails capture admission.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared Snapshot class and the resolved kind, components, and treatments the capture request names, all complete at capture admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live capture request, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a disagreeing class identity can be refused, because acceptance publishes the class. Q4: the offending act is the capture request. Added under L2.D0 to discharge the previously uncited TAXONOMY-27.

diagnostic.remediation: Declare a class whose kind, component set, external-storage state, secret treatment, compatibility envelope, quiescence, device state, portability, and Process handling all agree, or refuse the capture.

invariants.title: Driver reports Snapshot capture success without per-component durability evidence
invariants.statement: A driver reports a runtime Snapshot capture successful only after returning per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence for every component the resolved class marks required, and otherwise reports failure naming the exact missing component.
invariants.rationale: Q1: the facts are the per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence, which exist only after the capture executes. Q2: producing and decoding that native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the capture commit and the last point at which success can be withheld. Q4: the Core-side completeness rule is the other half of the seam, filed at `185` (`core`), whose rationale declared this counterpart and never filed it (L1.D20).

diagnostic.remediation: Return per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence for every required component, or report failure naming the exact missing component.
